The fifth, an 'amendment' by EO 12060, is quarantined by the queue itself with the code PREDECESSOR_NOT_EARLIER_THAN_ACTOR, and the held note under 5 U.S.C. 5317 dates EO 12060 to May 15, 1978, before EO 12076 was signed on August 18, 1978, so it cannot amend EO 12076; no held text of EO 12076 or of a later order cites EO 12060 as affecting EO 12076.

research_rationale:
EO 12076 (signed 1978-08-18; 43 FR 37161-37162, Federal Register of August 22, 1978) was read in full in the held govinfo text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12076.txt (PDF pages 15-16; heading Executive Order 12076 of August 18, 1978, subject Levels IV and V of the Executive Schedule; number, date and subject agree with the census register row). Its authority is Section 5317 of Title 5. Section 1-101 places 17 positions, items (a) to (q), in level IV of the Executive Schedule; section 1-102 places 14 positions, items (a) to (n), in level V; section 1-201 provides that nothing in the order terminates or otherwise affects the appointment of the occupant of a listed position who held it immediately before the order's issuance; and section 1-202 revokes Executive Order No. 11861, as amended. The order has no sunset, termination, condition or report clause. The dossier's three own-terms leads (two condition leads and one fixed-term lead) were read in the source-ladder text and come from other documents printed on neighbouring Federal Register pages (the public-inspection notice, the list of rules going into effect and a Governors' proclamation), not from the order. The preamble recites the authority and the purpose (to place two positions in level IV and to codify other positions) and commands nothing beyond the sections. Whole-order end: EO 12154 (signed 1979-09-04; 44 FR 51965, Federal Register of September 6, 1979; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12154.txt, PDF page 9) section 1-202 states 'Executive Order No. 12076, as amended, is hereby revoked.' It has no effective-date or delayed-effect wording, so the revocation is read as effective on signing. Later amendments, recorded as events and not ends under the owner ruling on strike-and-insert amendments (2026-10-21): EO 12099 (1978-11-17) deletes item 1-102(e), Director of Policy Review, Department of Defense, and inserts it as item (r) of section 1-101; EO 12111 (1979-01-02) deletes item 1-102(g), Assistant to the Secretary and Land Utilization Adviser, Department of the Interior, and inserts item (s), Counselor on Labor Management Relations, Department of Commerce, in section 1-101; EO 12119 (1979-02-14) deletes item 1-101(f), Assistant Attorney General, United States Attorneys and Trial Advocacy, Department of Justice, and inserts in lieu the Counselor on Legislative and Intergovernmental Policy, Department of the Treasury. Each moves or replaces a position, so the substance of those items changed; a human reviewer should note that. Clause 1-202 revoked EO 11861 once, on issuance; its first end is that performance. All other clauses ended with the order on 1979-09-04. The U.S. Code note under 5 U.S.C. 5317 held in jobs/theophilus-sources states that EO 12076, as amended by EO 12099, EO 12111 and EO 12119, 'was revoked by Ex. Ord. No. 12154, Sept. 4, 1979, 44 F.R. 51965', which agrees with the date and instrument. The quarantined relationship lead naming EO 12060 is explained in the conflict resolution.

savings.reason: Read EO 12076 and EO 12154 for savings or continuing effects. The revocation of EO 11861 by EO 12076 section 1-202 persists after EO 12076 is itself revoked, and appointments made under EO 12076 are not undone by its revocation; EO 12154 re-lists eight of the positions in levels IV and V and its section 1-201 protects their incumbents. These consequences accrued or were carried forward and do not keep EO 12076 operative after 1979-09-04. The placements of positions EO 12154 does not re-list ended with EO 12076; no held source shows another instrument placing them.
